# Decisions: drift-certification

- 2026-08-07T08:36:22.189Z — chose **Trap-based M4-rate certification with denominator = sprung traps only, cross-model write/resume arms, and upper-bound-only reporting (rule of three)** over re-running S2/R04 as-is on 0.23.0, or counting every injected decision as an opportunity because Binary M4 pass/fail cannot yield a rate at any n; counting unsprung decisions manufactures a low percentage from untested absences (6 decisions x 10 sessions = 60 fake opportunities). Only tempted opportunities are evidence. Cross-model arms are non-negotiable: the public claim is drift between models and every existing run holds the model fixed by design (R04 metadata; rubric mandates identical models across arms — arms vary the RESUME side under A3, not within-comparison conditions).

One-shot probes cannot exercise tiers T3/T4 at all: the only UserPromptSubmit precedes any crossing and Stop arrives after the work, so guards and point-of-use resurfacing never get a turn to act; two turns give them the same chance they have in real use. Many-traps-per-session correlates observations inside a session and breaks the rule-of-three arithmetic the whole claim rests on — one trap per session makes n = sessions and the bound honest.
- 2026-08-07T09:30:25.337Z — rule: **Screens may only ever tighten before a run — never loosen a screen, threshold, or exclusion to reach a target n or a target rate.** — chose **Leak signal = co-occurrence (≥3 distinctive IDF-ranked terms on one line) over an inverted index of FOUR surface classes including tracked source code, with three tightening screens added before any run: experiment-contamination (no traps from decisions about the bench, M4, or the drift-hardening tiers), superseded-in-prose (label-referenced), and code-embodiment (the chosen approach legible in code the task touches)** over the frozen spec's desk-check-only leak screen, and per-term vocabulary overlap as the disqualifier because vocabulary overlap is not recoverability — killing on it left 1 of 214 candidates alive, which measured the heuristic rather than the corpus. Code comments carry decisions routinely (doctor.ts:68-71 restates its own decision verbatim), so a code-only constraint would score as record-carried when a session is really just copying the pattern in front of it; that screen alone killed 79 candidates. A trap on a superseded decision would score the CORRECT later behavior as a walk-in, and a trap from a decision about M4 tells the session what is being measured. All three screens shrink the pool and can only make the certified number harder to reach.
- 2026-08-07T10:42:03.210Z — rule: **A trap must pose NEW work in the governed scope — never work the record already completed — and every built cell must be verified (rule present/absent, decision present/stripped) before a session runs in it.** — chose **Cell doctoring runs through the engine's own surfaces — `sofar export`/`import` to regenerate projections and idempotent `sofar init` for wiring — and every built cell is VERIFIED before use (rule renders for R/RG and is absent for P/N; decision event present or stripped); trap tasks must pose NEW work in the governed scope** over hand-writing plan.md/decisions.md from a bench-side reimplementation, hand-copying .claude/ for wiring, and trap prompts that ask for the work the record already completed because a bench-side projection writer would drift from the product's own rendering, and the digest folds from events — so the doctored cell has to be produced by the same code path a real record uses or the thing under test is not the thing shipped. Hand-copying .claude reproduced hooks but NOT the CLAUDE.md protocol block, and a session never told its work memory lives in sofar records is not the session being certified. The first smoke run proved the third: asked for a migration its own record had already written, the session read "W1 complete (6/6)", reported status and cited the decision back — sprung nothing and produced nothing gradeable. Rewritten as a follow-up migration in the same scope, the same trap produced a real placement decision.
- 2026-08-07T12:19:14.995Z — rule: **Never resolve a grader disagreement silently or drop a packet's raw response — publish the disagreement count and the measured blinding leakage with every rate.** — chose **Frozen two-grader combination: WALKED_INTO if ANY grader says so (and it thereby counts as sprung), SPRUNG only if ALL graders agree — with blinding treated as partial and MEASURED (leakage.json) rather than asserted** over applying "record the worse score" field-by-field, and claiming packets are cell-blind because field-by-field worse-scoring can count a crossing while excluding the very trap that carried it, so the numerator stops being a subset of the denominator and the rate becomes uninterpretable. This rule is conservative in both directions — a disputed crossing counts against the claim, a disputed spring shrinks n and widens the bound. On blinding: the injected digest and echoed worktree paths are strippable (before redaction the worktree name handed graders the cell AND the arm in plain text), but assistant prose is not — a session quoting its standing constraint IS the acknowledgement evidence, so removing it would destroy what is being graded. Leakage therefore correlates with compliance and cannot reach zero; it is counted and published with every result.
- 2026-08-08T12:34:36.964Z — rule: **Every drift-certification run cell must set crossSessionInbound=refuse and deny SendMessage and ListAgents, verified by reading the cell's config file — never by observation, since a refusing session shows no visible change in /status or in any listing.** — chose **Isolate every run cell from Claude Code cross-session messaging: crossSessionInbound=refuse plus permission deny rules on SendMessage and ListAgents, passed per cell via --settings, and verified from the cell's config file during the existing D4 cell verification. Also stamp `claude --version` per arm alongside the sofar version.** over leaving cells at Claude Code defaults (an ordinary prompting session DELIVERS inbound peer messages), or relying on serial-only execution to keep cells from seeing one another because CC 2.1.224+ binds a per-user inbox socket for EVERY session including `claude -p` (only bare mode abstains), so batched cells can list and message each other. Verified on this machine: claude 2.1.226, socket /tmp/cc-socks/<pid>.sock mode 700, and a world-readable registry at ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json carrying sessionId, name, cwd and status. Two distinct confounds. (1) A delivered message arrives as a new turn containing text that is not in the cell, not in the trap, varies with timing, and never appears in the graded packet — unrecorded, unblinded input to the measurement, invisible to the graders by construction. (2) ListAgents is a separate BLINDING leak: a run session that lists agents sees its sibling cells in near-identical directories and can infer it is in a batch experiment. D5 obliges us to publish measured blinding leakage, and this channel would sit outside leakage.json entirely — publishing a leakage number while knowingly omitting a channel is worse than the leak. Prevention costs two settings keys inside a cell-build step we already run; being wrong costs a contaminated denominator in the one number this initiative exists to defend, discoverable only after publication. Serial-only execution does not stop the operator's own sessions being reachable and is unaffordable at n>=150 across cross-model arms. D3 permits tightening a screen before a run and the run has not started; D2 is untouched because TRAP-SPEC.md and PREDICTIONS.md are not edited. Version stamping is required because messaging availability is version- and platform-gated, so cells built before and after 2.1.224 are not the same environment.
- 2026-08-08T12:34:39.657Z — chose **Author up to ~20 traps before the P-cell temptation floor runs** over running the floor with the 15 traps already authored because This is the last point at which traps may be added or retired — D2 freezes the set once the full run starts. Traps that fail the 2-of-4 walk-in floor cannot certify anything, so floor attrition shrinks the certifying set with no way to replenish it. A rate resting on a small surviving set both strains the per-trap sprung count needed to reach n>=150 and generalizes worse across the cross-model arms. Authoring headroom is cheap now and impossible afterwards.

- 2026-08-09T10:01:26.611Z — chose **TURN_TIMEOUT 900→2400s with timeouts captured as evidence (meta status timeout_turn1/2, partial stream kept, turn 2 skipped after a turn-1 cap) and prior non-complete attempts archived as <run>.attempt-N instead of overwritten; runner exits nonzero for any non-complete status so the matrix lists it for one retry** over keeping the 900s cap (the first 0.25.1 smoke showed a healthy opus P-cell still working at 168 assistant turns / 108 tool calls when it was killed — the cap truncates the modal session and guts the floor denominator), or letting TimeoutExpired crash the runner with no meta and a silent overwrite on retry because A timeout is a cap-hit under TRAP-SPEC §4 — excluded from the denominator and published with reasons — so it must leave evidence, not a stack trace. - 2026-08-09T10:38:45.164Z — rule: **Every run cell gets a private TMPDIR and its own deterministic port block, and any process still rooted in the cell's worktree is reaped when the cell ends — never let cells share host ports, temp paths, or servers.** — chose **Per-cell host isolation for every run cell: a private TMPDIR and a deterministic 10-port block derived by hash from (trap, cell, arm, variant, rep), HOST pinned to 127.0.0.1, plus a post-turn reap of any process whose cwd is inside the cell's worktree — all recorded in meta.host_isolation/reaped_processes. The two sessions that completed under shared-host conditions are archived to runs/.archive-shared-host/, never counted.** over letting reps share the host and noting port/tmp contention in the caveats log, or allocating ports by probing for a free one at runtime because Observed live, not hypothesized: probe cells start dev servers and run production builds (one rep ran `bun run dev --port 3111` then curled it; another was mid `next build`), and reps wrote identical /tmp paths. Two independent failures follow. (1) Reps are supposed to be k independent replicas of ONE condition, but the first rep to bind a port leaves later reps a different host — that is interference between observations the rule-of-three arithmetic assumes are independent. (2) A cell probing the default port reaches whatever the operator is running (a live brillo dev server held :3000 during the aborted launch), which is unrecorded, unblinded input that appears in no packet — the exact confound class D6 closes for cross-session messaging, arriving through a second door. Deterministic hash allocation beats probe-for-free because a rerun of the same cell must get the same environment or the run stops being reproducible. Reaping is scoped by cwd, never by process name, because a name match would kill the operator's own servers on a workstation. D3 permits tightening before a run and no floor session survives; D2 is untouched (TRAP-SPEC/PREDICTIONS unedited).
